notation.signal: x~N(0,C(p)), C(p)=sum p_k Q_k, y=A x+epsilon; epsilon~N(0,R) independent; S=A C(p) A^T+R. Q1..Q3 are normalized cos/sin real rank2, Q4 Nyquist rank1; DC=0; p>=0; a=MULT=[2,2,2,1], a^T p=8 known exactly.
notation.samples: K independent latent draws x_i, one stacked y_i per x_i. Multiple frames of one latent draw are correlated coordinates of one y_i, never K independent draws. R is noise covariance, K is sample count, to avoid N-name collision.
notation.fixed_candidates: B_j fixed independently of all confidence/selection y_i; W fixed. Risk R_j(p)=E||W(B_j y-x)||^2=v_j^T p+c_j; pair g_jk=d_jk^T p+b_jk. Evaluation applies selected B to a fresh independent latent draw.

representation.map: M:Sym(m)->R^4, (M L)_k=tr[L A Q_k A^T]. With an orthonormal symmetric matrix basis T_r, D_kr=tr[T_r A Q_k A^T], L=sum l_r T_r. This convention correctly counts off-diagonal entries; do not use unweighted triangular vectorization accidentally.
representation.necessary_sufficient: An unbiased quadratic estimate of gap over the full trace-simplex exists iff d belongs to range(M)+span(a), i.e. solve d=M L+eta a for symmetric L. This is equivalent to d annihilating ker([covariance map; a^T]). Without known trace omit eta.
representation.estimator: ghat=(1/K) sum_i y_i^T L y_i-tr(L R)+b+8 eta. E ghat=tr[L A C(p) A^T]+b+8 eta=d^T p+b. Symmetrize L explicitly. No target HR or true p is needed to construct L: use known A,Q,W,R and independently fixed candidates.
representation.known_trace_redundancy: For this stationary point-sampling family each observed diagonal is a^T p/8. Hence a is already in range(M) whenever at least one coordinate is sampled; eta does not increase identifiability rank. It can remove needless estimation of a known constant and reduce estimator variance.
representation.fixed_L_construction: Let P=I-aa^T/(a^T a). Solve P D l=P d for minimum Euclidean-norm l; eta=a^T(d-Dl)/(a^T a). Or use exact linear algebra and confirm residual. This minimizes ||L||_F among valid representations with free eta. It does not necessarily minimize actual Gaussian variance for unknown S or the joint Frobenius/operator concentration radius.
representation.optional_variance_design: If S0 is fixed from independent calibration, choose L to minimize tr[(L S0)^2] subject to exact matching; freeze it before confidence data. Choosing L using the same y_i invalidates the fixed-quadratic law unless separately justified. A convex norm objective can optimize the displayed worst-case radius with extra offline cost.
representation.numerical_residual: For r=d-M L-eta a, g=E ghat+r^T p. Under p>=0,a^T p=8, r^T p lies exactly in [8 min_k(r_k/a_k),8 max_k(r_k/a_k)]. Preserve this interval even for numerical residual, with outward roundoff. Dropping a nonzero residual destroys unbiasedness. A nonidentifiable gap can only be conservatively enclosed by adding this structural interval, not declared unbiased.

variance_and_concentration.exact_variance: For fixed symmetric L, Var(ghat)=2 tr[(L S)^2]/K=2||S^(1/2) L S^(1/2)||_F^2/K. tr[(L S)^2] is nonnegative even though L S need not be symmetric. Signal/noise means must be known zero for this formula; nonzero mean adds variance and bias terms unless properly handled.
variance_and_concentration.mgf_proof: Let H=S^(1/2)L S^(1/2) with signed eigenvalues lambda_r. K(ghat-Eghat)=sum_r lambda_r(chi-square_K,r-K), independent across r. For centered error Z, log E exp(t Z)=sum_r[-t lambda_r-(K/2)log(1-2t lambda_r/K)] <= t^2 V/K divided by (1-2|t| h/K), whenever 2|t|h/K<1, where V=sum lambda_r^2 and h=max|lambda_r|. Apply Chernoff separately to Z and -Z.
variance_and_concentration.oracle_tail: For t>0, P(|ghat-g| > 2 sqrt(V t/K)+2 h t/K)<=2 exp(-t) when exact matching holds. V,h depend on unknown S, so this formula alone is not a data-only certificate.
variance_and_concentration.computable_uniform_bound: If a predeclared deterministic bound S<=smax I holds, V<=smax^2||L||_F^2 and h<=smax||L||_op. Therefore rad(L)=2 smax||L||_F sqrt(t/K)+2 smax||L||_op t/K is a computable valid radius. For stationary trace8 point samples, C_ss=1 and tr(A C A^T)=m, so ACA^T<=m I and smax=m+||R||_op; iid R=nu I gives m+nu, also for repeated sites. This is conservative and relies on exact stationary/trace restrictions.
variance_and_concentration.all_pairs: For P=J(J-1)/2 nonzero fixed unordered pairs, use t=log(2P/alpha). Union bound yields simultaneous coverage >=1-alpha without requiring independence among pair estimates. If P=0 selection is trivial; if L=0 exact constant gaps need no stochastic radius.
variance_and_concentration.interval_with_residual: Each simultaneous gap interval is [ghat-rad+8 min(r/a), ghat+rad+8 max(r/a)], plus deterministic numeric bounds. For the reversed pair use exact negative endpoints rather than estimating independently. Gap(j,j)=0.
variance_and_concentration.confidence_vs_unbiasedness: The exact matching condition guarantees unbiasedness; the uniform covariance bound plus iid Gaussian law guarantees concentration. An unbiased estimate can still have large variance and yield nearly no certificates.
variance_and_concentration.noise_trace_uncertainty: R known is required. If an independent calibration gives |tr[L(R-Rhat)]|<=e_R and |trace(C)-8|<=e_tau, enlarge radius by e_R+|eta|e_tau and account for calibration failure probability. A plug-in R or an assumed trace8 learned from the same target data is insufficient.
variance_and_concentration.machine_scope: Floating matching residual and numerical eigen/norm computation require outward error bounds for certified machine results. CPU residuals below are diagnostics, not interval-arithmetic proofs.

data_only_fixed_L_alternative.bound: For fixed L=U diag(lambda) U^T, define tau=tr(|L| S)=sum_r |lambda_r| u_r^T S u_r. Triangle inequalities on S^(1/2)L S^(1/2)=sum_r lambda_r v_r v_r^T give sqrt(V)<=tau and h<=tau. Thus |error|<=2 tau [sqrt(t/K)+t/K] on the Gaussian tail event.
data_only_fixed_L_alternative.observed_tau_upper: Fix all pair L matrices first. Count D_eig=P*m directions (include zero-weight eigenvectors in the count for simplicity). Split alpha=alpha_var+alpha_quad. For each unit eigenvector, vhat_r=K^-1 sum (u_r^T y_i)^2 and qu=chi2.ppf(alpha_var/D_eig,K). By exact one-sided chi-square bounds, u_r^T S u_r<=K*vhat_r/qu jointly with probability>=1-alpha_var. Consequently tau_upper=K/qu*tr(|L| S_hat) bounds tau for all pairs.
data_only_fixed_L_alternative.radius: With t=log(2P/alpha_quad), rad_data=2*tau_upper*(sqrt(t/K)+t/K). Joint gap coverage>=1-alpha_var-alpha_quad. Add the structural residual interval and outward arithmetic error as above.
data_only_fixed_L_alternative.same_data_is_valid: The same fixed-L y samples can form tau_upper and ghat: union of the covariance-bound and fixed-quadratic tail failure events needs no independence. This does NOT allow choosing L from those samples; fixed L remains essential. No plug-in asymptotic variance approximation is used.
data_only_fixed_L_alternative.optional_minimum: Use min(rad_data,rad_uniform evaluated at the same t) plus residual bounds; on the joint good event both radii dominate the relevant error. Do not use different alpha accounting silently.
data_only_fixed_L_alternative.precision_limit: sqrt(V)<=tau can be loose and qu small at low K. Useful certificates are an empirical question on a new frozen cohort; algebra alone does not show superiority to LP.

safe_choice.rule: For each candidate j compute u_j=max_k U_jk with diagonal0. If min_j u_j<=tau, choose a minimizer and report tau-certified; otherwise abstain or report an explicitly non-certified fallback. With simultaneous coverage, selected fixed-rule population regret on fresh latent draws is <=u_j with probability>=1-alpha.
safe_choice.important_scope: This is not a realized per-image HR-error guarantee, not same-y conditional safety, and not arbitrary natural-image evidence. It assumes a single common p for iid latent draws. W can be full I despite rank-deficient A because the assumed covariance family, rather than arbitrary deterministic x, can identify gap functionals.
safe_choice.failure: If no exact representation exists, retaining structural residual intervals is mandatory. If they straddle zero as K grows, no unbiased-data-only ranking certificate is available from that phase for that pair within this model.

sampling_specific.same_cost: phase[0,1] samples sites[0,4,1,5]; phase[0,2] samples[0,4,2,6]. Both have m=4 noisy coordinates per latent draw and identical scalar measurement count K*m. Their signal sampling matrices both have rank4<n8.
sampling_specific.phase_01: Covariance lags0,1,3,4 span all4 spectral parameters; rank(M)=4. Every fixed gap d admits an exact symmetric L. The earlier elementary inversion remains valid.
sampling_specific.phase_02: Only lags0,2,4,6. c0 and c4 identify p1+p3 and 2p2+p4; c2=-p2/4+p4/8 adds p2/p4 separation. rank(M)=3, ker covariance map=span{(1,0,-1,0)}. Known trace has zero projection onto that kernel. Exact gap representation exists iff d1=d3.
sampling_specific.failure_pair: The fixed power2 versus power2_swap_k1_k3 candidates can have d1!=d3 in phase[0,2]. Their observation covariances/evidence are equal, but full-target risk can depend on k1/k3 allocation. Store actual matching residual, witnesses and persistent structural interval; never silently project d and call it exact.
sampling_specific.positive_and_negative: Phase[0,1] enables unbiased gap estimates but may have large ||L|| and require many draws; rank4 alone does not guarantee useful precision. Phase[0,2] can estimate gaps satisfying d1=d3, including projected-target risks, but cannot estimate all full-target gaps. Phase choice must be judged per candidate pair and cost, not merely on rank.

cost_and_prospective_protocol.offline: For m coordinates symmetric basis dimension r=m(m+1)/2. Factor the 4-by-r projected matching map once per phase; solve P pairs and compute fixed matrix norms. Generic SVD cost O(4^2*r+4^3); low-dimensional rank tests and candidate GP filter inversions are recorded separately.
cost_and_prospective_protocol.online: Computing each y^T L y costs O(m^2), hence O(K P m^2); alternatively accumulate sample covariance O(K m^2) and evaluate P traces O(P m^2). Storage O(m^2+P m^2), and observation storage can stream. No per-case LPs or spectral reconstruction is required for exact-match pairs; computing a sample covariance is allowed but estimating the full latent spectrum is unnecessary.
cost_and_prospective_protocol.comparison: Direct quadratic intervals target only relevant gaps; LP intervals use a joint feasible covariance family and nonnegativity and can be tighter. No analytical guarantee that quadratic intervals certify more often or dominate. Candidate count, independent draws, alpha, cost of bounds, calibration and fallback must match.
cost_and_prospective_protocol.new_data_requirement: Do not use old formal-v2 scores or draws as confirmation of this new rule. Freeze L/eta construction, residual policy, alpha/tau, pair count, phases[0,1]/[0,2], noise levels, K grid, RNG namespace and runtime budget before a new synthetic cohort; evaluation true p is read only after cohort selections are frozen.
cost_and_prospective_protocol.suggested_diagnostics: Matching residuals, exact structural bias intervals, predicted variance and fresh independent Monte Carlo variance, sign confidence coverage, certificate frequency, false certificates against analytical true population risks, regret/fallback severity, and end-to-end construction/scoring/memory costs. Retain all abstentions and failures.

novelty_and_classics.status: Unknown; this is a classical linear moment representation plus Gaussian quadratic forms, not a claimed new general theory.
novelty_and_classics.GSURE: Projected GSURE identifies risks for arbitrary deterministic signal only on observable subspaces. Here full W risk gaps may be identified even if A is rank deficient because a known stationary covariance family restricts the random-signal law. This difference in estimand/assumptions is not itself proof of novelty; covariance-restricted unbiased risk estimation and classical moment methods must be checked.
novelty_and_classics.robust_optimization: Adding residual uncertainty intervals and choosing by upper gap continues classical partial-identification/robust decision methods. Replacing LP by a fixed quadratic estimate reduces computational form but is not automatically scientifically new.
